post_native_path_screen.scope: Posthoc samples, including each initial state; no continuous-time clearance or collision-response proof. Native robot self-collision remains disabled.

route_observation.scope: Descriptive canonical observations from one exposed full-route body. Transfer duration and contact presence do not measure load or prove the cause of loss.

interpretation: All 216 worlds are valid recovery failures, without terminal or transient supported-upright dwell.
Sixty-two of 144 new-controller worlds improve on their fresh selected reference, but every gain remains below five degrees. These finite gains are retained, not promoted.

The full route observes contact acquisition and transfer commands, but all four transfer intervals lose their required replacement contact after 5 to 14 controller intervals. Each loses rotation; no transfer reaches its planned duration.
The transfer observation covers one exposed body. It does not measure ground reaction, isolate the cause of contact loss or establish behavior on the other bodies.
Successful route coverage, clear geometric endpoints and zero joint violations do not establish useful recovery or adaptation.
The raw progress shortlist is empty, so the declared path screen selects zero paths and grants no new clearance conclusion.
Reference-block assignments and these exposed morphology groups do not establish causal factor effects, held-out generalization or learned selection.
next_gate: Diagnose the four retained full-route transfers before another broad successor. Reconstruct the observed replacement-contact loss alongside resolved motor commands, joint protection, posture and requested versus observed actuator response. Contact presence is not a load measurement, and the cause is not isolated. Use the diagnosis to declare a distinct broad test of sustained replacement support and staged unloading, rather than merely retiming failed retractions. Keep fresh selected-reference comparators, original motor and joint bounds, the five-degree gain rule, full path screening and fresh full-capture varied-start confirmation. Actual recovery remains necessary for the same-body Studio walk-fall-recover-resume handoff; startup and stepping performance remain separate measured product work.
